Fresh to 3d printing and need a bit of guidance

I own a printrbot simple makers edition ( in kit ). ( so a PLA-only printer with a pretty small printing volume ).

I think the most important part that allowed me to understand the printer better was simply having to build the printer itself.

As long as the printer use G-code, you can use the software you find most confortable to you and I never had to use tech support so I can't really help there... ( The only real problem with my printer was it managed to corrupt its own firmware, but a quick read to the relevant wiki and I made it run on a enhanced one )

The main thing you'll have to learn is that a 3D printer is a tool, with its own tricks to make it work perfectly. Like preparing the printing bed, checking the calibrations, finding the correct temperature for the specific batch of plastic you use or learning the limits of your particular printer ( no two printers really work the same way ) and the plastic itself.

( Oh, keep an eye on the peachy printer. )

Anyway, knowing what I now know, I would have gone with a reprap : getting the parts is a pain in the ass, but for the same price as my current one, I would have been able to print in ABS and with a heated bed i would have avoided many print warping headaches.
awesome thanks this is a great help! Thanks for sharing your mistakes so others can learn from them :)

This seems like it was tailored to early internet users. Definitely speaks volumes about where the internet has gone in the past five years, though.

EDIT: I've been thinking about this, and the more I do, the more it feels like there's some pretty bitter irony in the way things have gone. The internet became popular (at least the way I see it) by offering an alternative to mainstream content sources, and it's gradually become the very thing it seeked to get away from.

So let's say for the purposes of arguing, between the TPP, whois privacy potentially going away, and all the other crazy/terrible ideas out there right now, things get really bad? Are you guys okay with starting over from square one?

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cjdns it is impossible for NSA or admob to profile users on a decentralized peer to peer network. I'm sure the mindless Facebook will return even on a P2P network but anonymized users are non-tracked users.

Edit: 2 words

With time, it's likely that they might develop a way to do it; they've definitely shown pretty considerable motivation to beat Tor. If I'm not mistaken though, with the TPP, web hosts would be responsible for user content anyway, so it might not matter - when they see questionable activity, they could quite potentially just have it removed, or at the very least, begin fighting portions of the internet that can't facilitate that tooth and nail.

My point is though, there's potential for things to get really bad. If they do, what's the alternative to the alternative?

The concept of a 'host' on a p2p network is not present. All peers are hosts. The people involved in cjdns hope to relegate commercial ISPs to 'cable pullers'. Alternatively, stringing a wire to your neighbors house, and/or wireless will suffice. Cjdns has been designed to replace the internet - not simply operate anonymously over it.

I encourage anyone interested to read up: https://github.com/cjdelisle/cjdns/blob/master/doc/Whitepaper.md

Think about it this way, early Internet adopters required pretty high literacy for most users to navigate anywhere meaningful.

Now, you need no computer (or regular) literacy to be in the cross hairs for the Metadata collectors. In fact, it's better for them if you don't even realize the basic function of a script because then you can't protect yourself. When the next gen of p2p launches it will be awesome until the same thing happens.

Human nature is the same as it was before the internet. As the media becomes more aware of it, content can be made and delivered efficiently.

Even if we start over it is going to end up in the same place because the behavior of the end users haven't changed.

Interesting reading for those who care to understand the details of congressional politics.

For legislators, cooperation is a form of political currency. They act in concert with other legislators, even at the expense of their own beliefs, in order to bank capital or settle accounts

So trading votes is how the business of politics is conducted. “Once you have promised another member that you will do something—vote a certain way, sponsor a particular bill, or conduct a hearing—you are committed to do it.”

As Frank has it, legislators have to act in ideologically inconsistent ways in the short run if they want to advance their larger objectives in the long run, as those larger objectives can only be achieved with teamwork. And the other members of their legislative team are only going to play ball with them if they know that they’ll take one for the team, that they’ll vote for something they don’t like because the team needs it.

I think my favorite games in the series are probably from the SNES era. You've already completed IV, V has great gameplay but not a very memorable story (as you already know) and it's a constant grindfest. VI has a good story, great villain, and also good gameplay.

From the PS1 era, I prefer VII and would recommend playing the original because I'm pretty sure the remake will be a "reimagining" of some sort. My brother loves IX but I never got into it, I might go back and try it again at some point.

However, the one I will recommend you play is X mainly because it will be a new experience for you, but also for the following reasons. That was my first game in the series and that might influence my opinion of it, but I pretty much love everything about it. Solid story that would honestly make an amazing movie (although I wouldn't want that, they would probably screw it up), amazing soundtrack, good gameplay, decent minigame if you're into that. There are some games in the series I've struggled with getting into or just took forever to complete for one reason or another. But I had trouble putting down X, and it's probably the game I've replayed most besides KH2.
